correctness.rationale: The main article uses the vaccination loss \(\nu_a\mathrm{VE}_a S_a\); the supplement derives its calibration from \(\nu_a(S_a-S_{\infty,a})\); and the released notebook implements the main multiplicative form. Solving the two scalar calibration equations gives distinct rate maps. With \(T=150\) and \(\mathrm{VE}=0.93\), the simulated law requires \(\log 2/(150\cdot0.93)=0.004968796993\ldots\) per day to halve susceptibility. The supplement rates instead yield final susceptible fractions \(0.1317636\ldots\) and \(0.0675749\ldots\), not \(0.165\) and \(0.11\). The checker independently recomputes these identities.

value.rationale: The mismatch changes the intervention parameter-to-target map: the supplement uses a positive asymptote and no vaccine-efficacy multiplier, while the simulated model uses exponential removal to zero scaled by vaccine efficacy. The resulting 150-day half-target rate is \(0.49688\%\) per day for both groups rather than the printed \(0.658\%\) and \(0.846\%\). Because reactive vaccination is one of the paper's main intervention levers, an exact correction to its campaign-intensity calibration is useful for reproduction, reinterpretation, and extension of the intervention scenarios.
